claims.claim: Last-move compression: if H is k-uniform and its classical Maker-Breaker duration τ(H)=t is finite, then θ(H)≤max{k,t−1}. More precisely, θ(H)=k when t=k, while θ(H)≤t−1 when t>k.
claims.evidence: A classical win on a k-uniform hypergraph requires at least k Maker moves, so t≥k, and any token-game win requires at least k simultaneous Maker tokens, so θ(H)≥k. Fix a classical strategy S winning within t Maker moves. During the first t−1 Maker moves, place fresh tokens according to S and maintain a virtual classical history whose Maker claims are exactly these token locations and whose permanent virtual Breaker claims contain every currently occupied actual blue vertex. After an actual Breaker placement or relocation, use its destination as the next virtual claim if virtually free; if it was already virtually blue, or Breaker passed, use any virtually free filler. Such a filler exists on every nonterminal branch: if no vertex remained after an earlier Maker move and Maker had not won, S could not still be a winning classical strategy. Thus S always prescribes an actually free vertex because the actual blue set is contained in the virtual blue set. Fresh Maker placements strictly increase her occupied set, so no repeated game state interrupts this simulation. If the branch first wins on Maker move t, S's vertex x completes a k-edge e whose other k−1 vertices are among the t−1 current red tokens. For t>k, exactly t−k or more current tokens lie outside e, so one can be moved to x without vacating e, giving θ(H)≤t−1. For t=k, k fresh placements implement S, and the lower bound gives θ(H)=k.
claims.search_method: Reconstructed the strategy invariant from the authorized game definitions and checked passes, relocations, virtual-filler availability, early wins, repetition, t=k, and t>k separately.

claims.claim: Uniform strict half-bound: every finite-theta k-uniform hypergraph H on n vertices satisfies θ(H)≤max{k,⌊(n−1)/2⌋}. In particular, if n≥2k+1 then θ(H)≤⌈n/2⌉−1.
claims.evidence: Finite θ(H) implies that Maker wins classically, hence τ(H)<∞. In any classical play on n vertices, Maker has made all of her possible moves by round ⌈n/2⌉, so a winning strategy wins by then and τ(H)≤⌈n/2⌉. Claim 0 therefore yields θ(H)≤max{k,τ(H)−1}≤max{k,⌈n/2⌉−1}. Exact parity calculation gives ⌈n/2⌉−1=⌊(n−1)/2⌋. If n≥2k+1, then ⌈n/2⌉−1≥k, so the maximum equals ⌈n/2⌉−1.
claims.search_method: Deductive implication from the independently checked compression lemma, followed by exact integer parity and threshold case analysis.

claims.claim: Exact order obstruction: a finite k-uniform hypergraph can attain θ(H)=⌈n/2⌉ only when n∈{2k−1,2k}; both orders are attainable.
claims.evidence: Let q=⌈n/2⌉ and suppose θ(H)=q. If q>k, Claim 1 gives θ(H)≤max{k,q−1}=q−1, a contradiction. If q<k, the simultaneous-token lower bound θ(H)≥k contradicts θ(H)=q. Hence q=k, which for integral n is equivalent to n∈{2k−1,2k}. For attainability at either order, take the complete k-uniform hypergraph. Fewer than k tokens cannot fill an edge. With k tokens, Maker makes k fresh placements. Before her kth turn, at most k−1 red and k−1 blue vertices are occupied, totaling at most 2k−2; because n is 2k−1 or 2k, a free vertex remains. Her k occupied vertices then form an edge, proving θ(H)=k=⌈n/2⌉.
claims.search_method: Exhaustive symbolic case split on the relation between ⌈n/2⌉ and k, followed by direct verification of the complete-hypergraph construction at both boundary orders.

target_evidence: The exact target asks whether some fixed k≥4 permits arbitrarily large equality examples, or otherwise for a uniform stricter bound. The verified estimate gives θ(H)≤⌈n/2⌉−1 whenever n≥2k+1, excluding arbitrarily large equality examples for every fixed k≥4. The exact obstruction further proves that equality is confined to n=2k−1 or n=2k and supplies examples at both orders, so the result is neither vacuous nor merely asymptotic and fully resolves the requested target. The draft's claimed resolution of FULL is therefore accurate.
